status: Development vectors for the FHT 1.0 contract (FHT-Specification#8). No FHT schema is released and no installed toolkit reads FHT yet: every expected outcome is derived from the rule text, never from an implementation under test.
fhtContract: fht.json — the generated FHT 1.0 development schema (specs/005-rna-transcriptome-header/spec.md)
checksumDefinition: base64(SHA-512/256) over the (decompressed) file bytes except the root-level checksum line and its terminator (docs/FORMAT.md R1-R5); written by scripts/make_fht_fixtures.py and cross-checked by scripts/check_fht_fixtures.py

R1.summary: Checksum rule 1: hash the exact file bytes without normalization; for gzip/BGZF input, the decompressed bytes. A line ends at LF, CRLF or a CR not followed by LF.

R2.summary: Checksum rule 2: exactly one root-level checksum line with an unquoted key; spaces only to match root indentation and before the colon; nested checksum properties (such as a derivedFrom parent checksum) stay covered.

R3.summary: Checksum rule 3: exclude that entire line and its terminator; hash every other byte, so changing covered bytes invalidates the checksum.

R4.summary: Checksum rule 4: SHA-512/256 digest in standard padded base64, no prefix; the encoding is canonical (the unused bits are zero) and checksums compare as exact strings.

R5.summary: Header parsing: the checksum line holds only the 44-character value, plain or quoted, with optional spaces; comments, tags, other text, block scalars and continuation lines are invalid.

R6.summary: Header parsing: FHT header lines are UTF-8 without U+0085, U+2028 or U+2029; bytes outside header lines are not decoded.

R7.summary: Header parsing: a FASTA file must not begin with a UTF-8 byte order mark.

R8.summary: Header parsing: no duplicate mapping keys, YAML anchors, aliases or merge keys.

R10.summary: Header parsing: header lines form the leading block before the first FASTA record; a ';~' line after that point, including one from a concatenated file, is invalid; ordinary ';' comments and blank lines may be mixed in around and inside the block.

R11.summary: Header writing (FASTA): header lines should not contain a raw '>' or '@'; writers escape them as \x3E and \x40 in double-quoted YAML scalars, which read back as the same characters.
R11.notApplicable: R11 is a writing recommendation: a raw '>' or '@' keeps the file valid and validators warn; the shared suite likewise has no invalid R11 vector.

R12.summary: Header parsing: YAML metadata is read with YAML 1.2 core-schema types and must read the same under YAML 1.1; explicit tags and plain scalars that the two versions read differently (010, 1_000, 1:30, yes, on, 1e3) are invalid.

R13.summary: Numbers: a numeric metadata value must be a finite number. YAML .nan, .inf and -.inf make the record invalid.

R14.summary: Links: a value whose schema format is uri should use http or https (ftp, urn, doi and info are also accepted); any other scheme stays schema-valid, but validators warn.
R14.notApplicable: R14 makes validators warn, not reject: an unexpected link scheme is schema-valid. Its valid vector carries "warnings": ["R14"].

R15.summary: Extension fields: from the FHT 1.0 development contract (FR-010), a top-level key matching ^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ may hold any value; every other unknown key and an x- key in a nested object stay invalid.

V1.summary: Schema selection: the raw-main FHT schema URL selects the reader's current FHT schema (here the 1.0 development contract).

V4.summary: Schema selection: a cited release the reader does not have, or that published no FHT schema, is unsupported-version; the file is not checked against another schema.
V4.notApplicable: V4 describes an outcome for citations the reader cannot resolve; with no FHT release, no valid vector cites a release URL, so V4 has no valid side.

T1.summary: FHT (provisional; text in conformance/README.md): the parsed header metadata must validate against fht.json — required fields, enums, patterns, nested cardinality and the closed top level (plus R15 extension keys).

T2.summary: FHT (provisional; text in conformance/README.md): a record's schema value must be a URL the FHT contract accepts (raw main, an FHT release tag or an FHT w3id URL). Another type's schema or an arbitrary URL fails fht.json; it never silently selects the FHT schema.

T3.summary: FHT (provisional; text in conformance/README.md): a derivedFrom parent checksum must equal the checksum recomputed over the supplied parent file's bytes; a mismatch is an invalid link (checked-fail), and a parent that was not supplied makes the link unchecked, never verified.

vectors.description: RNA transcript set (U alphabet); LF line endings; the checksum line is the last header line; plain scalars and mappings follow R8/R12.
CRLF line endings; CR bytes are hashed.
Lone CR line endings.
LF, CRLF and CR line endings mixed in one file.
The last sequence line has no terminator.
cDNA representation (T alphabet) of the same synthetic set: coverage is alphabet-independent (FR-006) and the supplied T bytes are preserved, not converted to U.
Exactly the nine required fields (FR-001); no optional field is defaulted or written null.

Ordinary ';' comments, blank lines and a ';~#' YAML comment around or inside the header block; a plain ';' comment after a record stays a comment (only ';~' lines after records break R10); all of it is hashed.
Every header line, including the checksum line, has root indentation 1.
Spaces before the colon on the checksum line.
The checksum line is first in the header block: R3 excludes the line wherever it sits, so the value matches fht-fasta-lf.
Trailing spaces on the checksum line are excluded with it.
The checksum value is a quoted single-line scalar; the key stays unquoted.
A root checksum line plus the indented nested parent checksum under derivedFrom: only the root line is excluded; the nested checksum is covered metadata (R2).
A header value holding '>' and '@' written as \x3E and \x40 in a double-quoted scalar; it reads back with the real characters.
Raw non-ASCII UTF-8 (U+00E9) in a header value is allowed; only U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 are excluded from header lines.

vectors.description: Top-level x- extension fields of every JSON type (FR-010, R15): string, integer, number, boolean, list (with null) and object.
A relatedLink URI with a non-link scheme stays schema-valid; validators warn (R14).
fht-fasta-lf compressed as one gzip member; the checksum covers the decompressed bytes and is unchanged.
fht-fasta-lf compressed as multi-block BGZF (with EOF block); same checksum.
The raw-main FHT schema URL with schemaVersion '1.0' selects the reader's current FHT contract — today the 1.0 development schema. The bytes are those of fht-fasta-lf under a stable V1 vector id.
A transcribedFrom FHR parent: the supplied parents/parent-genome.fhr.fasta recomputes to exactly the cited checksum (checked-pass). The accessionID is additional, not a substitute.
A filteredFrom FHT parent whose file is the fht-fasta-minimal vector, cited by its recomputed checksum (checked-pass).

vectors.description: A well-formed parent checksum whose parent file was not supplied: the record is valid and the link is unchecked — a reader must not report it verified and must not reject the record for the absent parent.

Every optional FHT field; vitalStats are genuinely computed from the vector's own sequence bytes; both permitted parent relationships cite the supplied parent fixtures' recomputed checksums (checked-pass); one extension field.

vectors.reason: Checksum computed after normalizing CRLF line endings to LF.
Checksum computed after U-to-T (RNA-to-cDNA) normalization of the sequence lines; the supplied bytes keep U (FR-006).
Checksum computed after upper-casing the lower-case sequence line.
A nucleotide changed after the checksum was computed (checksum mismatch); the metadata itself is untouched and still valid.
The value is standard padded base64 of a SHA-256 digest, not of SHA-512/256; exact-string comparison fails.
The value is SHA-512 truncated to 32 bytes and re-encoded; SHA-512/256 is a distinct algorithm, so the exact string differs (and the encoding may not even be canonical).
The final payload character is outside the canonical set AEIMQUYcgkosw048, so a 32-byte digest can never encode to it.
No root-level checksum line at all.
Two root-level checksum lines with the same value.
Only the indented derivedFrom parent checksum is present; a nested checksum never substitutes for the root line.
The checksum line is a YAML block scalar indicator ('|-') and the value sits on the next header line; R5 requires the value on the checksum line itself.
A checksum value continued on the following header line (a folded plain scalar); R5 allows one line only.
A YAML comment follows the checksum value; the line holds the value and nothing else.
A raw U+2028 byte inside a header line: YAML treats it as a line break (R6 excludes it; U+0085 and U+2029 behave the same way).
The file begins with a UTF-8 byte order mark; the BOM also removes the ';~' prefix from the first header line.
A duplicate root-level 'version' mapping key.
A YAML anchor on relatedLink reused through an alias on transcriptomeSynonym.

A ';~' line after the first FASTA record; it is neither ignored nor merged. (The stated checksum is consistent with the bytes, but a reader must reject the shape before the comparison stage, so this vector is classified 'unreachable'.)
Two complete FHT files concatenated; each part is internally checksum-consistent, but the second header block follows records (and adds a second root checksum line).
A plain integer with a leading zero: YAML 1.1 reads 011 as octal 9, YAML 1.2 reads decimal 11, so the value is ambiguous (the schema cannot see this — only the R12 rule rejects it).
vitalStats.averageTranscriptLength is the YAML .inf: not a finite number (type 'number' alone accepts it, so R13 is the rejection).
An x- key inside the nested taxon object: extension fields are top level only.

fair-bioheaders v0.5.0 published no FHT schema (the w3id URL is a 404 and the release registry has no FHT entry); the result is unsupported-version — not a check against another schema and not a silent fallback to raw main.

The child's bytes, metadata and self-checksum are all valid, but the cited parent checksum does not equal the checksum recomputed over the supplied parents/parent-genome.fhr.fasta (checked-fail): a verifier must report an invalid link, not treat it as unchecked and not pass it silently.
